content.en: Machine learning algorithms have been tested in various studies to determine their ability to predict outcomes and functional independence in patients with acute ischemic stroke. The results show that while machine learning algorithms can improve outcome prediction and accurately predict clinical outcomes, they do not always outperform traditional scoring methods or logistic regression models. However, machine learning models have shown good performance in predicting the clinical outcome of stroke and can provide valuable insights for clinicians.
content.da: Maskinlæringsalgoritmer er blevet testet i forskellige studier for at bestemme deres evne til at forudsige resultater og funktionel uafhængighed hos patienter med akut iskæmisk slagtilfælde. Resultaterne viser, at mens maskinlæringsalgoritmer kan forbedre forudsigelsen af resultater og præcist forudsige kliniske resultater, overgår de ikke altid traditionelle scoringsmetoder eller logistiske regressionsmodeller. Dog har maskinlæringsmodeller vist god præstation i forudsigelsen af det kliniske resultat af slagtilfælde og kan give værdifuld indsigt for klinikere.

critic.en: Imagine a world where your life is determined by an algorithm—and not even the most accurate one at that. Even if ML models show "good" performance, what about the cases where they don't? When it comes to healthcare, especially stroke outcomes, we must demand more than "valuable insights." We owe patients precision, reliability, and ultimately, trust. Are we ready to let "not always" define our standards?
critic.da: Så, vi skal bare acceptere, at maskinlæring kan forbedre outcome prediction, selvom den ikke altid overgår traditionelle metoder? Det er ligesom at sige, at en ny behandlingsteknik "kan" fungere, selvom den ikke altid er bedre end de gamle. Er det nok for dig?

potential.en: I believe that the use of machine learning in predicting stroke outcomes is a great example of how technology can make a significant impact in healthcare. These models have the potential to provide clinicians with valuable insights and help them make more informed decisions, ultimately leading to better patient outcomes. While it is true that machine learning algorithms may not always outperform traditional methods, their ability to improve outcome prediction and provide accurate insights is a step in the right direction. I am excited to see how this field will continue to evolve and how these models will be integrated into clinical practice.
potential.da: Forbløffende! Selvom maskinlæring ikke altid overgår de traditionelle metoder, er det godt at se, at der er fremskridt. Måske er det vigtigste, at vi nu har et alternativ, der kan give nye perspektiver for klinikerne. Jeg kan ikke lade være med at håbe, at disse teknologiske fremskridt en dag vil kunne redde liv og forbedre behandlingen for patienter med slagtilfælde.
